To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stability of graphene-based suspensions and the resulting photoactive hybrids can be tuned by the incorporation of phthalocyanin-based oligo(PPV) backbones of different lengths.
we have discovered a new class of graphene-based hybrid materials, which are photoactive and can be used as active components in solar cells.
oPPV-derivatives of zinc phthalocayanine (ZnPc) are able to interact tightly and reversbly with graphene and that the resulting hybrids show photo- and red-activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of graphene-based materials with controlled properties, such as electronic and optical properties and stability, by means of molecular design.
the preparation and characterization of novel hybrid materials that combine the electronic properties of phthalocyanin-based oligomers and graphene nanographene.

the synthesis of new phthalocyaninato-based oligomers and the investigation of their interaction with graphite to obtain stable suspensions of NG that can be used in the fabrication of novel photovoltaic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oPPV-1 and oPPV-2 do not show any significant interaction with graphite, whereas oPPV-3 and oPPV4 interact strongly with graphite and form stable and photoactive NG hybrids.

the NG/3 and NG/4 materials are the first examples of stable and repeatable photoactive and photoelectrochemically active graphite suspensions, that are based on a π-π-interaction between oPPV-derivatives and graphite.
the NG/4 hybrid represents an excellent starting point for the development of new photoactive materials for solar cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of graphene can be tuned by phthalocianine based oPPVs towards photoactive and redoxactive graphene layers.
oPPV oligomer-functionalization of graphene layers can be used to tune the electronic properties of NG, which is a prerequisite for their use in solar cell devices.
we have developed a new strategy for the synthesis of NG hybrids with a high degree of control over the layer numbers and the electronic coupling of the individual components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oPPV-derivative based NG hybrids represent a promising class of materials for the construction of photo- and redoxyactive devices.

the NG/4 hybrids are a new class of photoactive and stable materials for the construction of organic solar cells and that oPPV-derivatives of zinc phthalocianine are a new class for tuning the stability and the electronic coupling of the NG hybrids.
the stability and the electronic properties of graphene can be controlled by π-conjugated oligomers.
